draft.title: Maps and spatial technologies
card: shows natural and built features of an area, such as rivers, roads and towns. Contour lines join places of equal height, so they show the shape of the land.
a picture of Earth taken from space. It shows land cover and change over time, such as bushfire scars or the spread of a city.
a geographic information system stores data in layers on a computer. Layers such as rivers, roads and population can be placed over each other to find patterns.
Each tool shows where things are. A GIS goes further, because it can combine and analyse layers to answer a question.
draft.remember: Maps and images show where things are. A GIS also analyses layers together.

a.q: Which tool lets a geographer place layers of data over each other to look for patterns?
a.why: A GIS stores data in layers, so layers such as rivers and population can be combined and analysed. A satellite image shows the surface at one time, but it is not a set of layers that can be combined and analysed.
a.clue: Think about which tool works with layers.

b.q: Sam wants to see how far a town in western NSW has spread over twenty years. Which source suits this best?
opts: One topographic map showing contour lines
A single interview with a town resident
A table of last year's rainfall
b.why: Satellite images taken in different years show land cover and change over time, so Sam can compare the town's edge. A topographic map shows the land's shape and features, but one map shows only one time.
b.clue: Sam needs to compare the same place at different times.
